title: fix(runtime): a flow name two packages hold is refused at /automation with a remedy that works from there
body:
Fixes #23501
Clause-②: no

## What this does

A flow name that two packages hold is refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` at `/api/v1/automation`, because the door saves and deletes without naming a package. The refusal is correct, but the door relayed the metadata store's remedy as it was: "on the REST door add ?package= with the package id". `/automation` reads no `?package=`, so a caller who followed the remedy got the identical `409` again.

The answer is still `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. Only its remedy changes, and it now names a route that works from this door. No new error code and no new door input. The minting sentence in `metadata-protocol` is untouched, so it stays door-agnostic as triage ruled (`6171263447`).

| route at `/api/v1/automation` | remedy it now prints |
|:--|:--|
| `PUT /NAME`, `POST /` | `PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/NAME?package=` naming one of the listed packages, with the flow definition as the body |
| `DELETE /NAME` | `DELETE /api/v1/meta/flow/NAME?package=` naming one of the listed packages. It removes that package's row and keeps the others. |
| `POST /SOURCE/clone` onto such a name | the clone door's own taken-name refusal (`flowCloneNameTakenMessage`): a clone takes a NEW name, and the refusal suggests one |

The facts the protocol's refusal states are kept: nothing was written or deleted, the flow name, and the packages that hold it (sorted, first five, then a count).

Landing: `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` (`registerAndSaveFlow`, `unregisterAndDeleteFlow` and three new helpers: `flowPackagesRefusingWrite`, `flowPackageRefusalMessage`, `flowWriteRefusal`), its test, and one `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/runtime`.

## How the door recognises the refusal (H2): not by the text

Measured: the thrown value carries its ADR-0112 envelope and nothing else. The wire body is `code`, `message` and `httpStatus`. There is no `details` and no package ids (probe over the real stack below). So the door reads two facts, and both must hold before it rewrites anything:

1. the envelope is `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / `409`; and
2. the served flow list (`protocol.getMetaItems({ type: 'flow' })`, the read `GET /meta/flow` serves) shows rows of this name stamped with two or more distinct `_packageId`s. Measured on the two-package rig: both rows are listed, `_packageId` `com.qa.alpha` and `com.qa.beta`.

The protocol stays the one decider. The list read supplies the package ids the answer names. When the two facts disagree, the store's refusal is relayed exactly as before: fewer than two packages listed, a list read that throws, or any other envelope (which is never looked up). Six pins hold that half.

The cleaner long-term shape would be a structured carrier on the producer's refusal, such as `details.packages`, or a face-aware remedy like `destructiveChangeRemedy`'s `writeFace`. Both are `packages/metadata-protocol/src/**` edits, which are outside this card's surface: read-only here, and held by #23429's in-flight claim. See Acceptance notes.

## Measurements (real store: better-sqlite3, real `ObjectQL`, real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`, `HttpDispatcher.dispatch()`; tree `086fa4640`)

- **H1 holds.** `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal` (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:567`) mints the sentence. `PUT /NAME`, `POST /` and `POST /source_flow/clone` each answered `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with "...on the REST door add ?package= with the package id, in process pass packageId. Nothing was written. flow 'shared_flow' belongs to 2 packages ('com.qa.alpha', 'com.qa.beta')...". `DELETE /NAME` answered the delete wording.
- **The loop.** `PUT /automation/shared_flow?package=com.qa.alpha` and `DELETE /automation/shared_flow?package=com.qa.alpha` each answered the identical `409`.
- **H3, save.** `PUT /meta/flow/shared_flow?package=com.qa.alpha` answered `200` ("Saved flow 'shared_flow' (env-wide, package=com.qa.alpha, state=active)"), and only alpha's row changed.
- **H3, delete twin, which splits by transport.** On the dispatcher's `/meta` arm, `DELETE /meta/flow/shared_flow?package=com.qa.alpha` answered **`405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`** ("use GET, HEAD, PUT"): that arm serves no DELETE (`domains/meta.ts`, deliberately). On `RestServer` (`@objectstack/rest`, the `/meta` door `os serve` mounts), `DELETE /api/v1/meta/flow/shared_flow?package=com.qa.alpha` answers `200` and removes alpha's row only (pinned below). So the DELETE remedy names `RestServer`'s route. The changeset and the code comment say plainly that a dispatcher-only host (the `@objectstack/hono` catch-all) answers that route `405`.
- **H4.** PR #23499's pins assert `{ status: 409, code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT' }` only, never the remedy wording. None flips; all 10 still pass.

## Deviation from the suggested route (Zone 3): the clone

For `POST /:name/clone`, the remedy is the clone door's own taken-name refusal, not `PUT /meta/flow/NAME?package=`. A clone writes a NEW flow and carries no package envelope (ADR-0126 §7.1). Writing the copy into one package's row of a name two packages hold would be the same-name shadow that the clone door's taken-name refusal exists to stop. Followed as printed, the refusal clones under the suggested name: `200`, saved as a package-unbound row, and the two-package rows unchanged.

## Tests (`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-flow-door-package-address.test.ts`, extended)

Head `84124fefd`:

- **Remedy pins, both seed orders.** 4 routes × 2 orders = 8 tests. Each asserts `code` + `status`, the method and route the remedy names, and the two packages it states, then follows the remedy as printed: the method and path are read out of the answer, never restated by the test.
  - `PUT`: followed on both `/meta` transports, `RestServer` with alpha and the dispatcher's arm with beta. `200` each, and the labels land in the named rows.
  - `POST /`: followed on `RestServer`, `200`.
  - Clone: under the suggested name, `200`.
  - `DELETE`: followed on `RestServer`, `200`. Rows go from alpha and beta to beta only.
  - Loop controls: `PUT` and `DELETE` resent at `/automation` with `?package=` still answer `409`. This holds the message's "/api/v1/automation reads no ?package=" true.
- **Guard pins** (stub protocol, 6 tests). Each case is relayed as it was thrown: a `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` whose name the list shows in one package only, one whose list read throws, and a `409 METADATA_CONFLICT` whose list is never read.
- **Run.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2 src/domains/automation-flow-door-package-address.test.ts` gives `Tests 26 passed (26)`.
- **Package suite.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` gives `Test Files 381 passed (381)`, `Tests 5646 passed | 19 skipped (5665)`, exit 0.
- **Typecheck.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` exits 0. Its `check:test-typecheck` compiles the test layer (`tsconfig.test.json`) and held the identity-pinned debt ledger.

**Ablation** (subject is in-package `src`, so no `dist/` leg; every restore verified by blob hash equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`):

1. `automation.ts` restored to `086fa4640`'s blob (the verbatim relay): **8 failed | 12 passed**. All 8 remedy pins went red. On `PUT`, `POST` and `DELETE` the regex found no `?package=` route in the old sentence. On the clone, the old sentence contains `?package=`.
2. The guard's threshold lowered from two packages to one (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 to 0): **2 failed**. These are the two "one package only" guard pins.
3. The envelope check deleted: **2 failed**. These are the two "another envelope is never looked up" guard pins.

## Gates (run after the last commit, `7044dd98d`)

- Patch round 1 (`7044dd98d`, the round-2 `os-dev-report` `6182631933` on #23501): `pnpm check:durability-log-level` exits 0: "durability-degradation log levels: 46 durability-critical catch seam(s), all loud, rethrowing or propagating to the caller (7 propagating, declared)". It was red at `84124fefd`: the save catch in `registerAndSaveFlow` left through `deps.error`, which is not a declared failure-propagation callee. Every catch path now answers `deps.errorFromThrown(await flowWriteRefusal(...))`. The wire answer is unchanged. The derived 64 families were re-run at `7044dd98d`, all exit 0.
  - *(This line and the heading were rewritten by the `domain:cli` seat 1 PM, session `session_01FLwgbTSmGMrqsXkBDsiwfG`, as a read-modify-write of the live body. The dev does not PATCH a PR body. The bullets below are round 1's readings at `84124fefd`.)*

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **64** commands. All 64 ran locally, each exit code captured before any pipe. `--ran` reconciliation: "64 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 64 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".
- Of note: `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` 0, `check:error-status-conformance` 0, `check:route-envelope` 0, `check:system-context-census` 0, `check:doc-authoring` 0, `check:engine-double-contract` 0, `check:type-check-debt` 0 (its closure build ran under the verify lock).
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, other packages unbuilt). After `check:type-check-debt`'s full closure build it was re-run and exited 0. The re-run is the recorded reading.
- Lint (the lane blind spot): `pnpm exec eslint packages/runtime --no-inline-config` exits 0 with no output. `@objectstack/runtime` has no lint script of its own. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Dispatcher-only hosts cannot delete one package's row.** On such a host (the `@objectstack/hono` catch-all), `/meta` serves no DELETE (`405`, deliberate in `domains/meta.ts`, which names it as needing its own card). So on that host no door removes one package's row of a two-package flow, and the DELETE remedy printed here answers `405` there. It is loud, not a loop. On `os serve` (`RestServer`) it works.
  - Mounting DELETE on the dispatcher's `/meta` arm is a surface widening, not taken here. Carrier: none known.
- **The refusal carries no structure.** The producer's refusal has no package ids (`details`), which is why the door confirms by a list read. Carrier: none; this is not a defect.
- **The branch is two commits behind `main`, not merged.** The two commits are `7ffc57846` (metadata-protocol `reference-sites.ts`) and `b57228913` (a spec test). Neither touches the save, the delete or the automation door. CI runs on the merge ref.
- **Unmeasured inference: a clone onto a name one package holds.** If one package's stored row holds the name while the engine holds none, the clone door's collision probe asks only the engine, and the package-less save would resolve to that package's row. Not measured, not filed.
